key_insight: Stochastic mid-circuit measurements and conditional resets can drive a noisy quantum processor into non-equilibrium steady states that match theory and reveal equilibrium-like crossover behavior.
engineering_relevance: This work validates a practical hardware protocol for preparing collective stationary states on superconducting qubits, supporting future quantum algorithms that rely on mid-circuit measurement and reset.
method: Built a noisy discrete-time model with unitary gates interleaved with projective measurements and conditional resets.
Implemented the protocol on a superconducting quantum processor for up to 7 qubits.
Studied the interacting Floquet transverse-field Ising model as the test case.
evidence_signal: The stationary state predicted by the noisy conditional-reset theory agrees quantitatively with the experimental results on the quantum processor.
watch_item: Performance is limited by hardware noise in mid-circuit measurement and reset operations, which may affect scalability beyond the demonstrated qubit counts.
paper_title: Nonequilibrium steady states induced by stochastic mid-circuit measurements and resets on a quantum computer
